A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Antidistillation Sampling work. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v4 reports original distillation experiments on GSM8K, MATH, and MMLU, together with architecture comparisons, approximation checks, and loss analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds results using smaller and larger proxy models in Figure 11.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces its forward-difference estimator with a centered difference using proxy parameters θP±εg and denominator 2ε. This localized pseudocode correction aligns it with Equation 10 already present in v4; it does not establish a new sampling framework or that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, including GSM8K Platinum for testing, MATH, and MMLU. Figure 11 varies proxy model sizes within the retained GSM8K task rather than adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Temperature sampling, undistilled-student references, permutation sampling, and the JVP comparison are retained. Although v5 says it introduces permutation sampling, the same comparison already appears in v4 Appendix A and Figure 6. Figure 11 uses existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Figure 11 adds configurations pairing Qwen-2.5-1.5B and Qwen-2.5-7B proxies with a Llama-3.2-3B student, extending the previous 3B-proxy configuration. Existing data splits, accuracy evaluation, generation settings, and distillation schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 11 adds a focused robustness analysis testing whether antidistillation transfers when proxy and student parameter counts differ. Existing permutation controls, finite-difference checks, architecture comparisons, loss analyses, and example traces are retained.

E5.justification: The same means and 95% confidence intervals over bootstrapped LOWESS fits are documented in v4 Appendix B.2 and v5 Appendix D. No changed run counts, seed disclosures, or statistical testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds teacher–student accuracy curves for two proxy-size configurations, showing lower distilled-student accuracy with antidistillation than temperature sampling at comparable teacher accuracy. Existing results in Figures 1–10 and the example traces are unchanged; the additions concern new configurations.

T1.justification: The formal setup and derivations are retained. Centered finite differences already appear in v4 Equations 9–10 and 13, so the Algorithm 1 correction repeats existing mathematics. Changes to the temperature expressions are algebraically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about poisoning distillation while controlling teacher utility. The added experiment supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly interprets Figure 11 as evidence of robustness to proxy–student size mismatch. Section 4.1 also strengthens the interpretation of the unchanged permutation control, moving from evidence of useful gradient information to 'definitive evidence' that the computational overhead is necessary.

D1.justification: Figure 11 supplies explicit proxy and student model identifiers for the added configurations, modestly extending reproducibility information. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, software, and code-access information are retained. JVP precision, attention-kernel restrictions, and slowdown details are relocated into Appendix C.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. No cited work or novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: v5 shortens Section 4.3 by relocating JVP implementation discussion, reorganizes and renames appendix sections, corrects cross-references, and updates the conference footer. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the two-panel Figure 11 and its caption. Existing figure graphics are unchanged, while equation typography, a caption, and page flow receive limited adjustments. The example-trace displays are preserved on later pages.

improvement.justification: Figure 11 addresses a previously untested proxy–student size mismatch, strengthening evidence for practical applicability, and Algorithm 1 now agrees with the existing centered-difference equations. These are useful, bounded improvements. The stronger claim of definitive computational necessity exceeds what the unchanged permutation control establishes, tempering the overall benefit.
